tool.excerpt: Sudan: A War of Atrocities Report of the Independent International Fact-Finding Mission for the Sudan. This report documents attacks on civilians and objects essential for their survival in Sudan. It concludes that both parties to the conflict violated international human rights and humanitarian law, with most violations amounting to war crimes. The Rapid Support Forces’ conduct may also constitute crimes against humanity, including persecution and extermination. The report calls for accountability and sets out a roadmap for justice.

According to Sudan's Emergency Lawyers Group, a drone struck a crowded market on Saturday morning, killing 11 civilians and injuring dozens of others. The group said the raids are part of a continuous pattern of direct attacks on civilian infrastructure, constituting a grave violation of international humanitarian law. It called for an immediate cessation of hostilities and demanded accountability for those responsible. In a separate incident at the weekend, a drone reportedly belonging to the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) struck a fuel station in El Obeid, the capital of North Kordofan state.
